feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear senior-level positioning, credible progression, and relevant digital strategy depth. It reads professionally and is easy to trust, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, fewer repeated skill sections, and more outcome-focused achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing scope, leadership, and credibility.  
- Strong use of concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact.  
- Writing is polished and professional overall, with consistent tone and strong alignment to digital communications/strategy roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce redundancy across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and dilute impact. Consolidating them would improve structure and scannability.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; list punctuation is slightly inconsistent (e.g., “workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, and systems” style choices across sections); “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “French (A2, learning).” No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less repetition of skills already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior positioning and mission-driven/public-sector relevance.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a sharper value proposition tied to strategy, modernization, and operations.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial and operational workflow design, and audience-focused content strategy across web, email, social, and multimedia. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear communications, aligning stakeholders, and strengthening the systems that support large-scale advocacy and public-sector engagement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat language from Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination are reinforced throughout Work Experience; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-value strategic strengths over generic communication phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Multi-channel communication” with “Multi-channel communications leadership” for stronger, more senior positioning.
- Tighten overlapping workflow items by combining “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” into one clearer capability.
- Use more distinctive, role-relevant phrasing such as: Digital strategy & transformation • Enterprise web & CMS leadership • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production • AI-enabled search & content discovery
- Keep terminology consistent with the rest of the CV: use “communications” rather than “communication.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills, especially “Digital Strategy & Content Leadership” and “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.”
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new since returning as a consultant: advisory scope, platform improvements, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, content operations, and enterprise web improvements for member-facing communications.”
- Combine overlapping duties into 3–4 sharper bullets; e.g. “Redesigned Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and downloadable toolkits.”
- Emphasize outcomes where possible: adoption, efficiency gains, reduced publishing time, improved search/discovery, engagement, or fewer support issues.
- Recast technical work as impact: “Built workflows, analytics, and governance models that improved cross-team coordination and publishing consistency across web, email, social, and multimedia.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- CMS development/front-end troubleshooting may duplicate technical skills unless tied to a distinct project or result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management language already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more specific or measurable: add email open/click gains, audience growth, campaign performance, production volume, or cost/time savings from the in-house studio.
- Tighten analytics/governance bullets: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the consultant role and prior Associate Director entry.
- Video/programming language may duplicate the 2018–2022 and 2015–2018 NACo items unless this version stresses studio build-out and leadership impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and relevant scope, but this entry overlaps with the adjacent NACo roles and reads a bit generic. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and use action + outcome phrasing:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve alignment and publishing consistency.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows, increasing efficiency and content quality across channels.
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or stakeholder/team count supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- “Weekly video updates” is also mentioned in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/owning the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the most senior, recent strengths and use tighter, more distinctive phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with higher-signal, senior-level language tied to recent roles.
- Emphasize governance, platform modernization, and mission/public-sector communications rather than generic “content planning.”
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy & information architecture

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and partially redundant with editorial/workflow points; replace with a more differentiated capability like information architecture or content operations.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but this item is too broad and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to your current/most recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and de-emphasize older/less central platforms unless they are job-target relevant; consider dropping either SharePoint or Power Pages.
- Replace “AI-enabled search experiences” with a sharper phrase like “AI-enabled search and structured content retrieval.”
- If space allows elsewhere, attach outcomes to these skills in experience bullets rather than here (e.g., 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both sections.
- “CMS modernization” overlaps with Core Competencies and multiple NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for a senior digital role, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Make it more outcome-oriented and aligned to the recent NACo leadership work where you built analytics infrastructure and reporting.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + business value, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than eight separate fragments.
- Replace weaker phrases with stronger ones: “Leadership reporting” → “executive dashboards and decision support”; “SEO and performance analysis” → “SEO, UX and conversion/performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and decision support • SEO, UX and digital performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- Tool names here overlap with Technical + IT; this section should emphasize strategic application, not just software lists.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list rather than a senior, impact-oriented skill cluster. It also overlaps with recent NACo experience, so tighten it to emphasize production leadership and delivery capability.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tasks/tools to higher-value capabilities: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio buildout and operations,” “PTZ camera direction and switching.”
- Use more senior phrasing that matches recent roles: replace “Video production and editing” with “End-to-end video production and post-production.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “- End-to-end video production and post-production - Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery - PTZ camera systems and multi-camera studio operations - Broadcast-quality studio production”
- If space allows elsewhere, move specific platforms/equipment out of Topline Skills and keep this section focused on outcomes-facing capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media entry, so this skills item should stay concise, not descriptive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and “Core Competencies.” This section should either add specificity on level of use or be trimmed to avoid repeating stronger evidence already shown in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web Platforms & CMS Administration
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migration support, modular page building) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider dropping the weakest/least-used platform unless you can substantiate it elsewhere; a shorter, more credible list is stronger.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical capabilities.
- “Web & CMS administration” also appears in Core Competencies, so this item should add nuance, not just repeat names.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more implementation-focused and trim older/basic items unless they support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied capability, e.g. **Front-End & Technical Implementation**.
- Reorder by relevance/recency and group for clarity: **API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • JavaScript/jQuery • HTML5/CSS3**
- If accurate, add scope/impact in brief parentheticals: **Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting/performance)**, **GitHub Actions (deployment automation)**, **API integrations (CMS/data workflows)**.
- Consider dropping versioned/basic terms (**HTML5, CSS3**) or simplifying to **HTML/CSS** to save space and sound more senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** almost verbatim; differentiate this section as tools/platforms only, or remove repeated items there.
- **API integrations** and **workflow automation** are closely related to the Automation section; avoid repeating both without distinct context.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize the most relevant automation platforms and group general collaboration tools separately or remove them.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Project Systems
- Rewrite as: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana
- If these tools were used materially in recent roles, add brief qualifiers: Airtable (workflow/database systems) • Power Automate, Zapier (process automation) • Jira, Asana (project tracking)
- Move Slack, Teams, Basecamp, and Trello to a lower-priority “Collaboration Tools” line only if space allows; otherwise cut for concision

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills, so this section should stay lean and tool-specific rather than repeat capability claims
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are partially redundant as project-management variants; listing all four weakens impact unless each was used substantially

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email platform leadership, not just list vendor names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability + platforms: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance and add context where true: **Higher Logic (enterprise newsletters/member communications) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented: **Led email operations for newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials using Higher Logic; experience with Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys and Mailchimp**
- Only keep platforms you’ve directly administered/configured; otherwise use **familiarity with** for weaker tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Work Experience bullets about email newsletters; avoid repeating audience size here unless you convert the work bullets to broader leadership language.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, platform refresh, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house communications capacity.”
- Replace “high-impact” with measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams, frequency of video series, audience growth, or production volume.
- Clarify supervision: use “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” only if this was true people oversight; otherwise say “coordinated with” or “mentored.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item focused on launching/producing the series, while the later role covers scaling it.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo entries; here, specify foundational setup rather than ongoing operational improvement.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generically and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since this is an older role, keep it concise and focused on foundational impact.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement first: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Tighten the rest into one supporting clause: “Coordinated innovation and research projects that supported county-focused programs and policy initiatives.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications.”
- If possible, add one metric or scope detail: number of episodes, audience, stakeholder groups served, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize team leadership or strategy here; later positions demonstrate that progression better.
